tasks.short: Tell customers prices, shipping dates and delays, and discuss delivery problems.

steps.what: Find the customer's order, agreed prices and delivery address.
Check shipment progress and confirm the latest supported delivery date.
Compose an update using confirmed prices, dates and delay information.
Send the update and retain the correspondence against the order.
Discuss serious delays and agree recovery options within delegated limits.

tasks.design: Join order details in the {ERP} to shipment events in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with freshness and recipient checks. Configure approved templates and event notifications through the {EMAIL}; missing dates, conflicting records and requests for concessions go to the order clerk. A recovery brief supports the human conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order and shipment records often lacked reliable links, and staff manually checked dates before copying them into messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing notification settings and modest integration code can cover routine updates. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort without improving unreliable shipment data.
tasks.still_hard: An expected shipment date may not support a delivery promise. Sensitive conversations, compensation and conflicting operational updates still need people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a delay means to the customer and negotiate a credible recovery.

ambition.what: Proactive delivery-recovery calls before critical orders miss their promised date

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to troubled deliveries and recovery conversations. Pricing, compensation and contractual approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Agree service recovery options with an existing customer.
reach.learn: Customer priorities, service commitments and concession limits.

evidence.claim: Integrated tools can answer order questions and perform supported order actions.
Order-management software can import orders and synchronise stock.
Templates and event rules can handle factual updates; time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This describes a goods business with order records in the {ERP} and shipment records in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Routine messages repeat approved facts; they do not create new delivery guarantees or concessions.
Conditional recovery calls are averaged into today's task time. The communication channel shares differ from the weak mail prior.
Build ranges are working effort for one business unit. Access and consultation under national rules may add elapsed waiting time.
unknowns: Whether shipment events and delivery estimates are timely and distinguish confirmed dates from estimates.
Which customer contacts may receive each order's information.
Which commitments and concessions the order clerk may make.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Can the available interfaces distinguish dispatch estimates, carrier estimates and contractual delivery dates?
Which event and deduplication controls prevent contradictory or repeated customer messages?
new_work: Resolve stale or conflicting order and shipment records.
Maintain message templates, recipient rules and escalation thresholds.
Check failed sends and sample automated updates for accuracy.

tasks.short: Link incoming order documents to the correct record and retain a retrievable copy.

steps.what: Retrieve incoming order documents and attachments from the shared mailbox.
Match the document to the customer and sales order.

loop.input: Order document without a reliable machine-readable order reference.
loop.output: Candidate customer and order references with supporting source text.
loop.check: Require an existing unique order match, consistent customer identity and no duplicate document hash.
loop.stop: One extraction pass per document within a fixed input limit. Missing, conflicting or ambiguous references enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use exact identifiers first. Varied free-text attachments sometimes require reading to locate the reference.

steps.what: Save the document with its order reference and retention classification.
Update the separate filing tracker so colleagues can find the copy.

tasks.design: Capture documents from the {EMAIL}, use exact references to link them to the {ERP}, and retain the original in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop proposes references only when fixed parsing fails; the order clerk approves uncertain links before filing. Searchable order links replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} index.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent references and disconnected document storage made manual naming and parallel indexes convenient.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured capture, document hashes and record links handle most filing. Bounded extraction can recover references from varied documents without delegating record ownership.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate customer records, amended orders and retention exceptions remain difficult. GDPR access, retention and deletion requirements must carry across the linked records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting order histories and distinguish an amendment from a duplicate.
tasks.altitude: Routine filing largely disappears, leaving ambiguous references and record-quality checks. No new commercial decision rights follow from this change.

reach.task: Resolve duplicate customer records before linking new orders.
reach.learn: Customer identifiers, record provenance and controlled merge procedures.

evidence.claim: Order capture can read email and document orders, check rules and post to the finance system.
The allnex vendor case reports 70% touchless orders; this does not establish a filing savings rate here.
Exact matching, duplicate detection and configured retention can automate routine filing; estimates require validation.

assumptions: A sales order already exists; this task files its evidence rather than creating another order.
A separate {SPREADSHEET} filing index exists in this representative workflow; companies with integrated attachments omit that step.
Human approval applies to uncertain proposed links. Exact unique matches bypass that review.
Build ranges cover one mailbox and archive, including access and any consultation effort required under national rules.
unknowns: Whether original documents must be retained separately from order attachments.
How often references are absent, reused or inconsistent.
Whether the current archive supports immutable originals, retention rules and deletion controls.
Which roles may read, correct or merge order links.
research_questions: Can attachment links survive order amendments and archive migrations?
What extraction accuracy is achieved on representative documents with missing or conflicting references?
new_work: Review uncertain matches and document-processing failures.
Maintain extraction examples and reference validation rules.
Audit retrieval, access restrictions and retention execution.
Repair broken links and distinguish legitimate revisions from duplicate submissions.

tasks.short: Warn relevant teams when stock is low or incoming orders threaten available supply.

steps.what: Check stock on hand, reservations and expected receipts.
Compare open order demand with available supply and shortage thresholds.
Assess uncertain shortages and identify affected commitments and urgency.
Notify purchasing and fulfilment teams with affected items, orders and required dates.
Check acknowledgement and remind the responsible team about unresolved shortages.

tasks.design: Calculate time-phased available supply from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and open demand in the {ERP}, using existing shortage alerts where sufficient. A {WORKFLOW} routes deduplicated notices through the {EMAIL} and tracks acknowledgement. A {BI} view prepares uncertain shortages for human assessment without allocating stock or placing purchases.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, reservations and open demand were checked on different screens, while notices and follow-up lacked a shared case identifier.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock alerts cover simple thresholds. Small integrations can add time-phased comparisons, recipient routing and acknowledgement tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Inventory accuracy and receipt reliability determine alert quality. Deciding which customer commitment takes priority remains a commercial and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently sufficient stock is unusable, uncertain or already informally committed.

ambition.what: Daily delivery-risk triage with purchasing and fulfilment

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time chasing acknowledgements and more time explaining threatened commitments. Stock allocation and purchasing authority remain with the responsible teams.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of non-retail sales workers
reach.task: Recommend which threatened customer commitments require escalation.
reach.learn: Service priorities, stock reservation rules and replenishment constraints.

evidence.claim: Order-management software supports stock synchronisation, providing part of the required data foundation.
Time-phased shortage calculations, routing and acknowledgement tracking can use deterministic rules.
Today's shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The {SPREADSHEET} is used for cross-system shortage assessment, rather than as the stock ledger.
Notifications stay internal, despite the prior suggesting external action. Purchase orders and customer promises are outside this task.
Routine threshold breaches bypass human assessment; uncertain shortages receive it.
Build ranges include access setup and applicable consultation effort under national rules; approval waiting time is additional.
unknowns: Whether reservations, receipts and demand use compatible dates, units and item identifiers.
Which shortages require immediate escalation rather than a digest.
Who owns acknowledgement and resolution for each item category.
Whether existing stock alerts already cover the required calculation.
research_questions: Can the supported interfaces expose reservation changes without double-counting committed demand?
Which alert suppression rules reduce repeats while preserving material changes in shortage severity?
new_work: Maintain thresholds, routing and escalation timers.
Investigate stale inventory feeds and unreliable receipt dates.
Review repeated alerts and unresolved shortage cases.

tasks.short: Prepare and issue invoices, shipping documents and contracts from approved order information.

steps.what: Collect approved order details, customer billing information and shipment confirmation.
Prepare the invoice and check prices, quantities, tax treatment and totals.
Prepare packing lists and shipping documents from shipment details.
Assemble the contract using approved templates and the agreed commercial terms.
Review departures from standard terms and approve or return the contract.
Post the validated invoice and send it to the billing contact.
Release checked shipping documents to the fulfilment team.
Send the approved contract for signature.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to generate and release standard documents only after reconciliation and completeness checks pass. A deterministic generator fills approved contract templates from the {DOCS}; departures route through the {WORKFLOW} to the sales manager. The {ESIGN} receives only the approved contract version and verified recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document preparation crossed several systems, and template changes were maintained separately from order data and approval records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document generation handles invoices and shipping forms. AI-assisted coding makes template mapping and approval integration cheaper; no model is needed to calculate totals or select approved clauses.
tasks.still_hard: Tax exceptions, specialist shipping requirements and negotiated clauses require expert resolution. A contract approval must remain bound to the exact version sent.
tasks.human_edge: Spot when apparently standard paperwork creates an unintended commercial commitment and obtain the right decision.

ambition.what: Pre-dispatch document-readiness checks for customers with complex billing requirements

tasks.altitude: The clerk focuses on transaction readiness and document exceptions instead of rekeying. The sales manager retains approval of nonstandard terms; no new signing authority is implied.

reach.task: Prepare a standard commercial offer with complete billing and service terms.
reach.learn: Approved clause choices, acceptance conditions and escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Order capture can validate customer, stock and price rules before posting order data.
Rule-based document generation and version-bound approvals are established implementation patterns.
The proposed document controls, time shares and build ranges are planning judgements, not a documented case outcome.

assumptions: The shares describe a blended workload; each order does not require all three document types.
The sales manager's approval time is included in task time and is not counted as order-clerk time saved.
Standard contracts use preapproved terms. Only departures require the approval step.
Failed billing or shipping checks block release and route to the responsible specialist.
Build ranges cover standard documents for one operating entity, access setup and applicable consultation effort under national rules.
unknowns: Which invoice formats, tax treatments and shipping documents are required.
Whether issued invoices and signed contracts have reliable correction and version histories.
Which terms require sales, finance or legal approval.
Whether the current {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ESIGN} support the required release controls.
Which document recipients and signatories are authorised.
research_questions: Can supported interfaces bind approval to an immutable contract version through signature dispatch?
How should partial shipments, credits and amended orders reconcile across generated documents?
new_work: Maintain approved templates, clause mappings and billing validations.
Resolve blocked transactions with finance, fulfilment or legal specialists.
Monitor failed document generation and signature dispatch.
Verify that released documents match approved data and versions.

role.altitude: The week shifts from copying and filing to delivery recovery, transaction readiness and resolving conflicting records. Commercial commitments, purchasing and nonstandard terms remain subject to existing delegated authority.
reach: Sales representative of services: agree recovery options and prepare complete standard offers.
First-line supervisor of non-retail sales workers: recommend escalation of threatened customer commitments.
New accounts clerk: resolve customer identity conflicts that obstruct reliable order processing.
skills_to_grow: Trace order, stock, shipment and document records across systems.
Distinguish estimates from approved customer commitments.
Resolve exceptions using evidence and delegated authority.
Understand billing controls, document versions and retention requirements.
Maintain routing rules and evaluate automation failures.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a delivery and document assurance service that identifies threatened commitments early, prepares recovery options and gives customers a clear route to resolution.
